Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large, well-circumscribed, and homogenous opacity in the right upper lung zone. Crucially, the right hemidiaphragm is clearly visible and maintains a normal contour and position below the mass, ruling out phrenic nerve invasion (which would cause elevation). Additionally, there is no obvious distortion or displacement of adjacent mediastinal vessels to suggest invasion.
